name: streaming-gate-and-record
scope:
SOURCES. All of them are the full spec, and this scope restates none of it. "The contract" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/BUILD-store-module.md. "The README" is src-store/README.md; it wins where the two differ. The one form is src-store/softland/store/act.clj. "The implied spec" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/store-module/IMPLICIT_SPEC.md, with its open points as the contract's builder's rules 10 to 21 rule them.

THE HARD PART. The decision of one act against the record of its layer, as contract item 3 gives it to the streaming gate (implied spec, "Rules that hold for every operation (C1–C10)" and O1), and the record that this decision reads and writes (contract item 5). This stage works only with layers of the class streaming. The base, the microbatch depot and the microbatch gate belong to the stage microbatch-gate.

OPERATIONS OWNED. O1 of the implied spec, whole, with one case left open: X31 needs a made layer of the other class, and no such layer can be made before the next stage. The stage microbatch-gate closes it.

WORK DONE HERE FOR OPERATIONS THAT ARE OWNED LATER. O1 decides every kind of act, and it cannot be shown without the reads. So this stage does O3, O4, O5, O6, O7, O8, O9 and O10 of the implied spec, each as far as it holds for a layer, an act-id or a lock of the class streaming (for O3: the "Any other layer" of contract item 9). By the stage doc's rule on cross-cutting operations, each of them is owned by the stage microbatch-gate, which completes it for the other class.

WHAT THIS STAGE MUST FIGURE OUT. Each is named by its role. The shape, the place and the mechanism of each are the plan's.
1. The module and its classpath: contract "What to build" and "Classpath".
2. The streaming depot: contract item 1; builder's rule 4; implied spec C1 and C9.
3. The door's declaration, with its limits: contract item 2; README, decisions 2 and 3 of 6 October; builder's rules 12 and 20; implied spec "Things that can arrive on a depot". The next stage's gate checks what arrives against this same declaration.
4. The digest: builder's rules 1 and 11; implied spec C6. The next stage's gate uses this same digest.
5. What the streaming gate does with a stray, and the state that this needs: builder's rule 10.
6. The checks of the decision, their order and their words: contract items 3, 7 and 9; builder's rules 2, 3, 8 and 12 to 17; implied spec C4, for the checks that the plan places. Contract item 4 gives the next stage "the same checks".
7. The record of a streaming layer: each part that contract item 5 names, and the room that each part leaves (contract "Not in this build, by decision"; README "Open, and built to a working answer", with point 4 of implied spec "Where the contract and the README differ"). What binds it: implied spec C2, C3, C5 and C8, and "Entity State × Write Matrix" E1 to E5. The last sentence of builder's rule 13 is for this stage's plan to answer.
   This record is the stage's interface to the next stage. For a layer whose facts are "across tasks" (contract item 4) it must make achievable: contract item 4, "Same record shape"; builder's rules 6, 7 and 18; README, decision 5 of 7 October, "a gate reads on its own task"; implied spec O2. This stage does not meet those requirements. Its record must not shut them out.
8. The stamp, and the state that it needs on a task: contract item 6; README, decision 4 of 8 October; builder's rule 17; implied spec C7, "The stamp (edge cases of C7)" and E6. X22 and builder's rule 18 are the next stage's; the stamp that is made here must make them achievable.
9. Locks and the seal: contract item 7; builder's rules 5, 15 and 16; implied spec O6, O9 and E4.
10. The reads of implied spec O8, O9 and O10 (contract item 8 and builder's rule 11; contract item 7; contract "The proof", "reads the class"), and the state by which a gate tells a layer's class from the layer's id (builder's rule 7). They are built here for the class streaming, in a form that the next stage can complete for the other class under builder's rule 7 and contract item 8.
11. The proof's hand, and each SHOWN line of contract "The proof" that needs neither the base nor the microbatch gate.
12. What the plan must find out or say for this gate: the last point of implied spec C7; implied spec X16 and X29; builder's rule 21.
13. The explanations of each part that is built here: contract "Explanations, as the tree's rules say"; builder's rules 8 and 14.

name: microbatch-gate
scope:
SOURCES. All of them are the full spec, and this scope restates none of it. "The contract" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/BUILD-store-module.md. "The README" is src-store/README.md; it wins where the two differ. The one form is src-store/softland/store/act.clj. "The implied spec" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/store-module/IMPLICIT_SPEC.md, with its open points as the contract's builder's rules 10 to 21 rule them.

THE HARD PART. The microbatch gate: the decision that the stage streaming-gate-and-record built, now "over a batch, across tasks" (contract item 4), for a layer of the class microbatch. What makes it hard is in builder's rule 6 and in implied spec O2, "Consistency and correctness" and X32 to X42.

OPERATIONS OWNED. O2 of the implied spec. And, by the stage doc's rule on cross-cutting operations, each operation that the earlier stage did for the class streaming and that is completed here: O3 (the base of contract item 9), O4, O5, O6, O7, O8, O9 and O10. At the end of this stage each of them holds whole, for both classes and for an act-id on either depot (implied spec X107), and the earlier stage's checks still pass. This stage also closes the one case of O1 that the earlier stage left open, X31, together with X41, the same case seen from this gate: builder's rule 7, in both directions.

WHAT THIS STAGE MUST FIGURE OUT. Each is named by its role. The shape, the place and the mechanism of each are the plan's.
1. The microbatch depot, and what it derives from an act: contract item 1; README, decision 10 of 6 October; builder's rule 4; implied spec C1, for any thing that arrives, and C9.
2. The order in which the acts of one batch are decided: builder's rule 6; implied spec O2, "Consistency and correctness" (its "one order") and X32 to X40.
3. How an act that "touches several tasks" is "accepted whole or refused whole" (builder's rule 6), and how the decisions of one batch are "visible together" (contract item 4): implied spec C3, as O2 carries it across tasks.
4. The record of a microbatch layer, in the shape that the earlier stage gave (contract item 4, "Same record shape"; contract item 5), and how the gate on each task, and each read, reaches what belongs to the layer as a whole: its class, its permissions, its locks, its answers. What binds it: builder's rule 7; README, decision 5 of 7 October, "a gate reads on its own task"; contract item 7, "how a lock that was asked for ahead comes to sit beside its value is the plan's"; the last sentence of builder's rule 6; implied spec O2, for the hops that the plan counts.
5. The stamp of a microbatch act: builder's rule 18; implied spec X22, E6, and O2 on the stamps and the order.
6. What the microbatch gate does with a stray, and the state that this needs: builder's rule 10.
7. The reads of implied spec O8, O9 and O10, completed for a layer, an act-id and a lock of the class microbatch: contract item 8; builder's rules 7 and 11.
8. What the plan must find out or say: builder's rules 9 and 19, with implied spec X42; builder's rule 21 for this gate; implied spec O8, "Throughput", for the reads that one microbatch act costs.
9. The rest of the proof: each SHOWN line of contract "The proof" that the earlier stage could not show; then the proof whole, run as the contract says.
10. The explanations, complete: contract "Explanations, as the tree's rules say", with the sections of the module's README that it names.
